name: Clapping Hands
baseMeaning: A picture of two hands meeting at the wrist, short motion lines at the sides. Read in a message it lands as applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice.
tldr: 👏 Clapping Hands. In a chat it comes across as applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice.

contextMeanings.meaning: The plain reading: two hands meeting at the wrist, short motion lines at the sides. Nothing hidden in the drawing itself.
Borrowed as a reaction, it reads as applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice.
contextMeanings.example: Reacting to a post that deserves a slow clap 👏

contextMeanings.meaning: In a dating thread the gesture is usually doing the work of a line that was not typed. It arrives as applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice, softened by whatever sentence sits next to it.

In a work channel it is read the same way it is read anywhere else — applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice — but the stakes of a misread are higher, because the sender is often talking about somebody's actual work.

platformNotes.note: In Slack 👏 lands in channels where the sentence was supposed to be shorter. It is usually standing in for congratulating someone on a win, and a channel where the topic is somebody's workload is where it misreads.

On Discord 👏 is a staple of the reaction bar, which is why it so often arrives stripped of its applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice reading — a shape pressed rather than a message sent.

On X and Twitter 👏 does most of its work in replies, where it tags a message like reacting to a post that deserves a slow clap. Short enough to survive being the whole post, which is exactly why it is used that way.

On iOS the Clapping Hands 👏 renders as the neutral drawing, and the neutral swatch is what most people send without thinking about it. A message like congratulating someone on a win is the kind that carries it — the picture lands before the sentence does.

WhatsApp renders 👏 exactly as the phone system does, but the keyboard keeps it in the hand section, where nobody looks unless they are hunting for it. In family threads it tends to accompany a message like reacting to a post that deserves a slow clap.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z reaches for 👏 to do the work of congratulating someone on a win, and treats the neutral drawing as the default rather than as a choice. What they hear first is applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice.

Millennials tend to send 👏 deliberately, usually for something like reacting to a post that deserves a slow clap, and they read applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice into it more often than the older cohorts do.
Gen X mostly uses 👏 literally, as the picture of the gesture itself, and is less likely to read applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice into it than younger senders are.
Older senders use 👏 in the most straightforward way, on family and group messages, and are less likely to hear the applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice subtext in it.

warnings.title: 👏 and 🙌 get swapped
warnings.description: The Raising Hands 🙌 is one tap away in every picker, and it does not carry the same reading — raised hands read as celebration and relief, clapping hands read as judgment or acknowledgement of something just shown. Check which one you actually picked.

warnings.title: The reading it usually gets is not the one it was sent with
warnings.description: People take 👏 as something else fairly often: it gets assumed to be sincere applause when the single-emoji version is more often ironic applause — praise for something everyone knows was a mess, and a lone clap gives it away. The sentence around it is usually what settles the meaning.

seoTitle: 👏 Clapping Hands Emoji - What It Actually Means in Text
seoDescription: 👏 Clapping Hands meaning: applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice. How the emoji is used at work, at home and in dating threads, and where it goes wrong.

longForm.overview:
The drawing of 👏 is two hands meeting at the wrist, short motion lines at the sides. It arrived with Unicode 6.0 in the hand section, and in a conversation it does the work of a line somebody left out on purpose.

The line it stands in for is applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice. That is the reading most people arrive with, and it is usually the intended one — a picture carries the same meaning as the sentence it replaces, and it arrives first.

The complication is that the drawing invites a second reading. It gets assumed to be sincere applause when the single-emoji version is more often ironic applause — praise for something everyone knows was a mess, and a lone clap gives it away. In practice that second reading is not rare — it is the one that decides how a message lands, because the sender has usually not thought about it at all.

It also sits in the crowded part of the picker. The nearest neighbour is 🙌 Raising Hands: raised hands read as celebration and relief, clapping hands read as judgment or acknowledgement of something just shown. The two are close enough that a fast thumb picks the wrong one, and the message goes out carrying a meaning nobody chose.

The clapping hands also exists in five skin tones. They are separate pages with separate copy, because picking a tone is a decision in a way that picking the plain emoji is not: it says something about who the sender thinks the reader is.

In short — the clapping hands reads as applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice, it is most often used for congratulating someone on a win or reacting to a post that deserves a slow clap, and the five tone pages under it each say something different about who is sending it. The rest of the page takes those three apart.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
Context, not the picture, decides how this lands. 👏 in a work thread is reacting to a post that deserves a slow clap; 👏 in a family thread is congratulating someone on a win; 👏 in a thread with somebody you like is a way of saying something you would rather not type out.

The tone versions of the emoji make the same point from the other side. The gesture is identical in all five, and the swatch says something about the sender before a word is read.

The shortest messages are the risky ones. A lone 👏 is the whole reply, and it is carrying a meaning nobody wrote down — applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice is the intention, but what arrives is a drawing. Everything the sentence would have disambiguated is simply missing.

Put it this way. Congratulating someone on a win is the job the clapping hands does most: it saves a sentence and lands faster than one would have. Reacting to a post that deserves a slow clap is the job it does second: there the picture is not the point, it is the temperature of the message.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Think about what the emoji is replacing. If the sentence under it is doing the real work, 👏 will get assumed to be sincere applause when the single-emoji version is more often ironic applause — praise for something everyone knows was a mess, and a lone clap gives it away instead, and the thread ends up carrying a meaning nobody wrote.

And keep it away from first contact. There is nothing warm in the drawing, and a clapping hands gesture used to answer other people's messages tends to sound like it is settling a point.

Keep it out of the formal register. In a thread about somebody's work, or in a message to somebody you have not met, 👏 reads as applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice, and formality is exactly where that reading does the most damage.

Leave 🙌 Raising Hands for the other message. Raised hands read as celebration and relief, clapping hands read as judgment or acknowledgement of something just shown. And keep 👏 out of threads where somebody is hurting: it reads as applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice there, because there is nothing in the drawing that says you meant well.
longForm.howToReply:
The safe move in an unclear thread is to answer the text. 👏 gets assumed to be sincere applause when the single-emoji version is more often ironic applause — praise for something everyone knows was a mess, and a lone clap gives it away often enough that the sentence matters more than the picture.

And do not send 👏 alone when the message underneath is supposed to be warm. A message like congratulating someone on a win carries the feeling; the picture on its own leaves the reader choosing between applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice and something sharper.

Start by reading what the 👏 was doing. If it was a reaction, react: 👏 back, and the thread is closed. If it was aimed at you, write. The difference matters, because the reply to a reaction can be a picture and the reply to a request cannot.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 👏 and its skin-tone versions?
faqs.answer: The tone variants under clapping hands show the same gesture in five different skin tones. The gesture does not change, but the tone is a small signal about who the sender imagines the reader is, and in some groups that signal is read louder than the sentence.

faqs.question: What does 👏 mean in text?
faqs.answer: 👏 is used for applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice. The drawing shows two hands meeting at the wrist, short motion lines at the sides, and that part is not in dispute — what changes is whether the sender is being literal or borrowing the gesture for a reaction.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 👏 and 🙌?
faqs.answer: Raised hands read as celebration and relief, clapping hands read as judgment or acknowledgement of something just shown. The two sit close together in most pickers, so the difference is often about which one the sender pressed rather than about what they meant.

faqs.question: Is 👏 rude?
faqs.answer: It can be. The gesture is meant as applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice, but it gets assumed to be sincere applause when the single-emoji version is more often ironic applause — praise for something everyone knows was a mess, and a lone clap gives it away. The risk is highest when it is the only message in the thread — a sentence gives the picture some context to sit in.

faqs.question: What does 👏 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: Nothing gender-specific. The same reading applies whoever sends it, and the meaning is set by the thread and by what is written next to it rather than by the sender.

conversationExamples.interpretation: A public sign-off, with the emoji as the full stop. The picture is doing the punctuation, which is why it is sent instead of a sentence.
The everyday use: the picture carries the whole line. It lands as applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice, and matching it with the same emoji is a normal reply.

conversationExamples.message: reacting to a post that deserves a slow clap 👏
conversationExamples.interpretation: A handover or a sign-off in a channel. It reads as applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice, and naming the next step in words is usually clearer than leaving it to the gesture.

conversationExamples.message: there is something you should know 👏
conversationExamples.interpretation: A small joke or a nudge, with the emoji doing the tone work. It gets assumed to be sincere applause when the single-emoji version is more often ironic applause — praise for something everyone knows was a mess, and a lone clap gives it away more easily here than it does in a work thread, because the thread is thinner.
Family threads are where this lands most naturally. The reading is applauding, or marking that a thing deserves notice, and nobody in the thread is reading it as anything sharper than that.
